scope: Row-by-row review of the complete reserved INFO and reserved FORMAT tables, reconciled with the immediately governing prose, subsequent field definitions, examples, labels and cross-references. This is an author review record, not independent approval or implementation conformance.
method: Every data row is captured with exact source line, ID, Number, Type, description and a contextual semantic disposition. Table metadata/continuation headers are excluded from data-row counts. The row-level interpretation is checked against the full local source context recorded below.

reconciled_semantics.finding: Reserved keys are optional conventions; a row in a reserved-key table does not mean every record/sample must carry the field. When emitted, metadata declaration and the reserved definition govern its schema and interpretation.

Number=A is ALT-ordered per alternate allele; Number=R is REF plus ALT ordered; Number=1 is scalar; Number=0/Flag is presence-only; Number=4 is a fixed four-value vector. Preserve these distinctions per row.

END is explicitly deprecated but retained for backwards compatibility. When present it is computed as the maximum end reference position across REF, symbolic SVLEN and <NON_REF> FORMAT LEN contributions; it is used for BCF rlen/indexing. This is not a blanket rule that END is required.

If genotype information is present, the same FORMAT key types/order apply across samples in the record; GT, if present, is first; if any local-allele field is present, LAA must be present and precede fields other than GT; no FORMAT keys are universally required; paired global/local representations must agree or one be missing/omitted.

Number=G values are ordered over nondecreasing allele-index tuples for ploidy P and N alternate alleles, with inclusive loop bounds. The specification supplies nested-loop and recursive algorithms plus the combinatorial index formula; GT ploidy determines P when GT exists, while diploidy is assumed without GT. Worked examples are informative cross-checks, not substitutes for the algorithm.

LAA contains distinct 1-based ALT indices and defines local allele membership and order; REF is implicit as local allele zero. LAA is required when local fields carry data. Local A/R/G fields map to the matching global field over the local allele universe. BCF zero-length vectors are encoded as missing; a missing-valued LAA is treated as an empty vector (REF-only) under the stated condition. Number=LA implementation-defined fields cannot preserve zero-length versus missing at REF-only sites.

M fields are fractions in [0,1]; DPM counts reads able to detect the modification; ADM counts reads with the modification. Regex-matching names are reserved even for invalid ChEBI IDs. Alias names map to specific ChEBI-keyed fields. Type=M fields are intrinsically stranded; ADFM/ADRM are not reserved. Unstranded CpG is represented at C with subsequent G missing; stranded CpG uses both positions, C encoding ADF and G encoding ADR. Reference-block values apply to all applicable covered bases. Example rows remain informative.

GT separators are allele-level phasing indicators; first indicator may be omitted and is inferred from the remaining indicators. PSL has one element per GT allele, unphased alleles map to missing entries, names are globally meaningful across CHROM, and PS and PSL cannot co-occur or interoperate. PSO disambiguates derivative-copy traversal; PSQ aligns one quality value per PSL phase set.
1000G is only a reserved INFO flag labelled 1000 Genomes membership in this VCF table. It is not evidence that any 1000 Genomes producer/project convention is normative VCF syntax.

LA is A restricted to ALT alleles selected by LAA; LR is R restricted to REF plus selected local ALT alleles; LG is G over the local allele universe; P has one value per allele value in GT; M has one value per possible base modification for the corresponding ChEBI ID. These definitions control cardinality and cannot be inferred from the one-character code alone.

Number=M cardinality is determined by GT and possible modifications for the corresponding alleles. The key suffix identifies modifiable base(s); U is synonymous with T; any base-modification key requires GT. Values follow eligible base positions on either strand and GT allele order; N modifications encode positive then negative strand; unphased allele values aggregate at the first occurrence; missing and symbolic alleles contribute no relevant bases. Unstranded values use the lowest-POS base with other values missing, with N modifications on the positive strand.

unresolved_questions: The reserved tables are not exhaustive of all legal custom fields; metadata-defined arbitrary fields remain allowed subject to VCF grammar and metadata declarations.
The row review does not establish implementation support, parser correctness, or laboratory qualification.
